archive.description:
About pplwise
pplwise is a recruiting consultancy for fast-growing technology companies across Europe. Through Recruiting as a Service and Executive Search, we fill key roles for our clients, from start-ups to publicly listed companies. We are filling this position for our client Filics.

About our client: Filics
Filics is reinventing intralogistics with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that change how material moves. Its double-runner system makes Filics the first and only AMR that can drive through load carriers such as Euro pallets. This breaks with forklift logic and sets a new standard for efficiency. Filics is a small, hands-on team that solves hard problems with engineering excellence. Leadership goes to those who take initiative and consistently deliver. As Electrical Engineer (m/f/d) at Filics, you will design the electronics at the core of the next generation of robots.

About the role
This is an on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to engineering and assembly.

Filics doesn’t just use off-the-shelf components. It builds its own custom IP. The robots run on advanced boards that cover a wide range of electrical engineering. On one end is high power, such as battery and motor controllers. On the other end are high-speed interfaces like PCIe, USB and MIPI CSI. The real challenge is making all these subsystems work together as one system. Many of these problems have no textbook solution. Solving them takes solid experience, a deep understanding of the physics and a creative mind.

The EE team is small, and the robot is far from finished. You’ll own your boards end to end: requirements, system design, schematic, layout, design review, sourcing, manufacturing, testing and validation. You’ll keep owning them for as long as they’re in production. You’ll work closely with Embedded Software, Mechanical Engineering, Software and the Production team. As Filics moves from prototypes to series production, your designs need to work reliably at scale, not just in the lab.

What you’ll do

  • Take full ownership of a complex PCB project and get it running in as few revisions as possible

  • Design high-power and high-speed circuits and make sure they work together at system level

  • Design for EMC, manufacturability and testability, and take boards through EMC testing and certification

  • Bring new technical approaches to the team, for example a new converter architecture that enables higher charging power in a smaller package

  • Introduce useful processes from your experience, such as simulation workflows that validate a layout before it goes to production

  • Help with board bring-up and debugging together with Embedded Software, and support Production with clear documentation and training

  • Take over ownership of existing boards so the team shares responsibility

About you

  • Several years designing electronics in an R&D environment at a smaller hardware company driven by innovation (e.g. robotics, e-mobility, aviation, autonomous vehicles, motion control)

  • A proven record of taking PCBs within a larger system from requirements to a validated product

  • Strong skills in schematic design and PCB layout (Altium, KiCad, OrCAD or similar)

  • Hands-on debugging experience with an oscilloscope, logic analyzer, VNA or spectrum analyzer, plus soldering

  • Experience with designs that went through EMC testing or CE certification

  • An innovator’s mindset: you have built something new or significantly improved an existing concept

  • Basic simulation know-how (e.g. LTspice, ANSYS, thermal/EM/tolerance analysis); deeper experience is a strong plus

  • Basic experience with Linux and embedded software

  • You work independently, take ownership and thrive without rigid structures

What Filics offers

  • Real ownership of your designs, from first draft to series production

  • Space to innovate and a wide range of technical challenges, from power electronics to high-speed design

  • A small, high-caliber team with close collaboration across disciplines

  • Fast growth: one year at Filics teaches you what usually takes many years at a large company

  • An on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to Engineering and Assembly

Sound like you? Apply with your CV.

archive.description:
About pplwise

pplwise is a recruiting consultancy for fast-growing technology companies across Europe. Through Recruiting as a Service and Executive Search, we fill key roles for our clients, from start-ups to publicly listed companies. We are filling this position for our client Filics.

About our client: Filics

Filics is reinventing intralogistics with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that change how material moves. Its double-runner system makes Filics the first and only AMR that can drive through load carriers such as Euro pallets. This breaks with forklift logic and sets a new standard for efficiency. Filics is a small, hands-on team that solves hard problems with engineering excellence. Leadership goes to those who take initiative and consistently deliver. As Senior Hardware Engineer – Mechanics (m/f/d) at Filics, you will lead the mechanical design of the robots as they move from prototype to series production.

About the role

This is an on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to engineering and assembly.

Filics builds its own robot hardware in-house: mechanics, electronics and software. Orders are growing, and the robots are moving from prototypes to series production. Designs that worked in the lab now need to be built reliably, at scale and at the right cost. The hardest problems often sit between disciplines: parts that work on their own can fail once they're assembled with the electronics.

The mechanical team has four engineers, most of them at the start of their careers, and they need someone who guides them every day. You'll be the technical lead for the mechanical side of the product and the counterpart to the electronics lead, so the current mechanical manager can focus on core R&D. Your time splits roughly evenly between hands-on engineering and technical leadership. You'll work closely with Electronics, Production, Procurement and the CTO, and you'll set the engineering habits while the team is still small.

What you'll do

  • Mentor the mechanical engineers day to day: help them make design decisions, set methods and keep projects focused

  • Design parts and assemblies in CAD, including tolerancing, and check every design for manufacturability and cost before it goes out

  • Lead testing and integration of mechanics and electronics, and solve the problems that only show once everything is assembled

  • Prioritise incoming work, follow up on progress and make the day-to-day technical calls on the mechanical side

  • Make the gated design process work in practice and run design reviews (safety, mechanics, electronics, manufacturability) before parts are integrated

  • Put design for manufacturing and design for cost in place: fewer, standardised parts and production methods that scale

  • Work with the electronics owner of each robot module from the first prototype on, and with Production on manufacturability and production jigs

  • Build and iterate prototypes based on customer and field feedback

About you

  • Several years of hands-on mechanical design in R&D at a company that develops and builds its own electromechanical products (e.g. power tools, home appliances, e-mobility, production machines, robotics, marine propulsion)

  • A proven record of taking an electromechanical product from prototype to series production (ideally 1,000+ units a year) on a fast development cycle of about a year, not a decade-long program

  • You still design hands-on in CAD, mainly metal parts and assemblies, with strong tolerancing skills (any CAD tool; Onshape is a plus)

  • You've applied design for manufacturing and design for cost, and cut cost through design: fewer parts, standard parts

  • At least two years of mentoring or technically guiding other engineers; a team-lead title isn't required

  • Experience testing and integrating mechanics with electronics

  • You've introduced processes, design reviews or engineering standards that helped a team deliver

  • You handle unclear requirements and break complex problems down so others can work on them

  • German is a plus, since production is mostly German-speaking

  • Bonus: GD&T and tolerance stack-ups, design of production jigs, or projects with motors, motor controllers or electronics

What Filics offers

  • A key role at an early stage: shape both the mechanical team and the product

  • Real ownership of the mechanical side, from first prototype to series production

  • A mix of hands-on engineering and leadership, with a path into team lead and engineering management as Filics grows

  • Fast design cycles driven by customer and field feedback

  • A small, high-caliber team with close collaboration across mechanics, electronics, software and production

  • Fast growth: one year at Filics teaches you what usually takes many years at a large company

  • An on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to Engineering and Assembly

Sound like you? Apply with your CV.

archive.description:
Bei GALVANY ist es unser Ziel, klimaneutrales Wohnen für alle zur Realität zu machen. Wir setzen auf Umsetzung und entwickeln konkrete, smarte Lösungen, indem wir Wärmepumpen, Batteriespeicher und Smart Metering einfach zugänglich, zuverlässig und bezahlbar machen.

Wir sind ein profitables Greentech-Startup und glauben, dass nachhaltiger Impact und langfristiges Wachstum nur auf Basis eines gesunden Geschäftsmodells möglich sind. Um unsere ambitionierte Tech Roadmap umzusetzen haben wir im Frühjahr 2026 eine Seed-Finanzierung in Höhe von 10 Millionen Euro mit Set Ventures und AENU abgeschlossen. Getrieben von Kundennutzen, Klarheit und Verantwortung stehen wir für hochwertige Heizlösungen und ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem Menschen Verantwortung übernehmen und nachhaltigen Mehrwert schaffen.

Die Rolle

In unserer Eigenproduktion bauen wir die Komponenten vor, die unsere Installationsteams beim Kunden direkt einsetzen: hydraulische Cubes und elektrische Unterverteilungen für die Wärmepumpe. Je besser sie vorgefertigt sind, desto schneller und sauberer läuft die Installation vor Ort.

Cubes sind unsere vormontierten Hydraulikmodule, die alle wesentlichen Komponenten für den Heizkreis kompakt in einem Gehäuse bündeln. Wir fertigen sie in mehreren Varianten für unterschiedliche Wärmepumpen und Einbausituationen.

Unterverteilungen sind die elektrischen Verteiler, über die die Wärmepumpe abgesichert und angeschlossen wird. Sie werden nach Plan in Standardvarianten je Geräteserie und Leistungsklasse aufgebaut.

Du arbeitest in einem kleinen Produktionsteam innerhalb von Supply Chain, eng verzahnt mit Lager, Kommissionierung und Einkauf. Die Produktion wächst mit unseren Installationszahlen und zieht 2027 in unser neues Hauptlager in Ludwigsfelde.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Montage von Cubes: Rahmen aus Aluprofilen aufbauen, Komponenten einsetzen, Verrohrung in Edelstahl-Pressfitting und Gewinde herstellen, Verkleidung montieren.

  • Aufbau und Verdrahtung von Unterverteilungen nach Bestückungsplan, Stückliste und Stromlaufplan, inklusive Beschriftung der Betriebsmittel.

archive.title: Technical Product Manager
archive.description:
About SANOVIO

SANOVIO is the collaborative AI platform for healthcare procurement. Every euro a hospital loses in purchasing is missing in patient care. We help hospitals get good products at fair prices, with far less manual work.

We build the software. And we move the goods. SANOVIO aOS, our agentic operating system for procurement, handles master data management, portfolio management and digital procurement processing. SANOVIO Fulfillment covers global direct sourcing, quality control, warehousing and logistics.

Founded in 2024 in Munich by Noel Nosswitz, Alexander Hüttner and Yong Wang, we work with hospitals in Germany and Switzerland, purchasing groups and international suppliers. We are customer-funded: our customers are our only investors.

The role

As Technical Product Manager, you turn real procurement problems into working software. You sit between our hospital and supplier users, our engineering team and the founders. You decide what we build next, shape how it works, and often build the first version yourself.

You work on SANOVIO aOS and the internal tools behind our fulfillment operations: AI agents that clean item master data, workflows that move an order from request to ward, and integrations with hospital and supplier systems.

A large part of the role is talking to customers. You join calls and on-site visits with hospital purchasing teams, purchasing groups and suppliers, show them what we build, take their feedback and turn it into product decisions. You are a trusted contact for our customers on everything technical.

Location: Munich (on-site, with flexibility).

What you will do

  • Own the product roadmap for selected areas of SANOVIO aOS, from problem discovery to release.

  • Be in close, regular contact with customers: hospital buyers, purchasing groups and suppliers, plus our own operations team, to understand how procurement works in practice.

  • Lead the implementation of SANOVIO aOS at customers: from setup and data onboarding to go-live.

  • Own product education: run trainings and onboarding for customers and our internal teams, and create guides and demos.

  • Write clear product specifications and translate them into tasks engineering can ship.

  • Understand and map user flows end to end, and find where users lose time or get stuck.

  • Iterate fast: ship a first version, learn from real users and improve it within days, not months.

  • Design and prototype AI agents and LLM-based features, for example matching products across supplier catalogues or checking certificates.

  • Automate internal workflows across procurement, quality, warehousing and finance, and connect the systems behind them.

  • Define how we measure success for each feature and follow up after launch.

  • Make sure what we build is secure, reliable and handles confidential hospital and supplier data with care.

Technical Skills

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including practical experience with Python, APIs, databases and modern development tools.

  • Hands-on experience developing AI-powered applications using large language models, AI agents and related technologies.

  • Experience implementing workflow automation and integrating different software systems and data sources.

  • Understanding of software architecture, data processing, deployment and the development of reliable, maintainable applications.

  • Familiarity with information security, access management and the responsible handling of confidential data.

  • Experience with modern AI-assisted development tools and an interest in continuously expanding your technical expertise.

What else you bring

  • A degree in computer science, engineering, business informatics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Graduates are welcome, as are candidates with 1 to 2 years of work experience.

  • A background in consulting (for example strategy, tech or operations consulting) and a strong pull towards AI: you build with LLMs and agents yourself, not only in slides.

  • Experience in product development: you have taken a product or internal tool from first idea to something people use every day.

  • Experience in customer-facing work: you enjoy presenting to customers, running workshops and explaining a technical decision to a hospital buyer as clearly as a business problem to an engineer.

  • You take ownership, work in a structured way and are comfortable when things are not yet defined.

  • You are AI-native: you use AI tools every day and follow what is new in the field.

  • You care about healthcare and want your work to have a visible effect on patient care.

  • Fluent English and German at C1 level or higher, as many of our customers work in German.

What we offer

  • A real problem with a direct effect on patient care.

  • AI that acts: you ship agents that do real work in procurement, not demos.

  • Software and logistics in one company, so you see your product used from order to ward.

  • A lot of responsibility from day one, real ownership of your area and short paths to the founders.

  • An office in the heart of Munich.

How to apply

Apply here with your CV and your LinkedIn profile. A link to your GitHub, portfolio or personal website is optional.

About Tritium Fuel Cycle (TFC)

GFG is designing a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) fusion power plant (FPP) to deliver 1 GW of electrical power in the 2040s. The “GIGA” plant will be based on a stellarator magnetic confinement fusion device, operating continuously on a deuterium-tritium (D-T) fuel cycle.  Prior to this, the smaller “Gauss Industrial Demonstrator (GID-170)” will be deployed in the mid-2030s.

While deuterium can be extracted from seawater, tritium is a tightly controlled radioactive isotope with an extremely limited global supply. Therefore, both GID-170 and GIGA must utilise closed tritium fuel cycle infrastructure, to ensure that unburnt tritium is fully recycled back to the stellarator and not released to the environment. Meanwhile, the tritium consumed by the fusion reaction must be replenished using tritium breeding blankets (TBB).

A first-of-a-kind dedicated tritium fuel cycle (TFC) facility, suitable for continuously supporting a stellarator device, must be designed, built and commissioned. It will adopt a multi-loop process architecture, each loop comprising many deeply integrated subsystems. Developing such a facility presents unique engineering challenges: the supply chain is still emerging, commercial process simulation tools lack dedicated TFC libraries, suitable off-the-shelf equipment is not always available, and some technologies have relatively low technology readiness levels (TRLs). 

A conceptual design is currently under development, with the project then progressing into pre-front-end engineering design (pre-FEED) in 2028, followed by front-end engineering design (FEED) and design for manufacturing phases. Completion of the overall design phase (for GID-170) must be achieved by 2032.


About the role

GFG is looking for several Tritium Process Engineers to join the TFC department and develop the GID-170 and GIGA TFC facilities. The roles will contribute to the continued development and optimisation of the overall fuel cycle architecture and its subsystems. Activities will include managing design requirements; developing process flow diagrams (PFDs), piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), heat and mass balances (HMBs) and the Basis of Design (BoD); selecting technologies; sizing and arranging equipment; and contributing to safety-related design. The roles may also involve supporting equipment prototype development and testing with technology developers and research partners.
We welcome candidates with complementary strengths in process design and process modelling and simulation, with systems engineering experience also desirable. These specialisations sit within the same engineering function, and candidates are not expected to have equal expertise across all areas. The number of appointments and balance of responsibilities will reflect the successful candidates’ experience and technical strengths. Drawing on their specialist expertise, successful candidates will work collaboratively on design development, modelling, analysis and optimisation to assess design alternatives and inform robust, well-documented design decisions.
The TFC comprises a wide range of technologies and subsystems, requiring the department to manage multiple sub-projects and work packages in parallel. Each engineer will contribute across several activities and will be expected to take ownership of specific tasks or subsystems, or lead work packages, depending on their experience. The roles will involve close collaboration with engineers from the same and other disciplines at national and international partner organisations, research institutions and suppliers, as well as with colleagues across disciplines and departments within GFG. Given the specific challenges associated with tritium, close collaboration with Nuclear Safety and Export Control specialists will also be essential.
During conceptual design, successful candidates will work closely with the Head of Tritium Fuel Cycle to address the strong interdependencies between subsystems and develop a coherent, integrated design. As the project moves into pre-FEED, they will be expected to take greater day-to-day ownership of their assigned areas and drive design development through pre-FEED and FEED, while maintaining close coordination across subsystem interfaces. As the project progresses, the roles will evolve to support design for manufacture, procurement and commissioning of the GID-170 TFC systems, followed by further development and refinement of the TFC design for GIGA.


Main responsibilities

  • Process definition and systems engineering
    1. Identify, define and manage system requirements and interfaces across TFC subsystems and the overall plant architecture.
    2. Develop and optimise the fuel cycle architecture, assessing alternative subsystem technologies, their respective advantages and disadvantages, technology readiness levels (TRLs), and potential system configurations.
    3. Develop process flow diagrams (PFDs) for individual TFC subsystem blocks and the overall plant architecture.
    4. Participate in the development of piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), identification and sizing of key components, and equipment layout.
    5. Develop and maintain representative heat and mass balances to support process definition, system integration and design decisions.
  • Process modelling and simulation
    1. Develop, apply and improve process simulation models for individual TFC subsystem blocks and the overall plant architecture, using tools such as Aspen Plus, Aspen Custom Modeler, Python and dedicated proprietary software, as appropriate.
    2. Support the development and integration of custom models and, where appropriate, contribute to the development of dedicated simulation tools.
    3. Use modelling and simulation to assess system performance, compare technology options and operating configurations, support component sizing, and inform process optimisation and design decisions.
    4. Documentation of assumptions, uncertainty and applicability limits, and perform model validation when suitable data becomes available.
    5. Work collaboratively with internal and external modelling specialists to ensure consistency between simulation results, engineering requirements and the evolving plant design.
  • Cost, safety and risk management
    1. Identify and manage design risks, developing effective risk-reduction strategies and action plans.
    2. Identify applicable standards, regulations and codes, and ensure that these are considered throughout the design process. 
    3. Participate in hazard, safety and accident analyses, including hazard identification (HAZID) and hazard and operability (HAZOP) studies, and contribute to the definition of safety functions and development of the safety case.
    4. Contribute to capital and operational expenditure (CAPEX/OPEX) estimates.
  • Design development and delivery
    1. Develop design documentation and specifications, including contributions to the Basis of Design and design philosophies.
    2. Document design studies, verification and assessment activities, engineering assumptions and design decisions.
    3. Support the design development, procurement and testing of prototypes for key components, in collaboration with technology developers, suppliers and research partners.
    4. Provide engineering support for R&D activities conducted in-house and with external partners and collaborators.
  • Project coordination and collaboration
    1. Lead specific technical tasks or work packages assigned by the Head of TFC, in line with experience and expertise.
    2. Take ownership of specific subsystems throughout the pre-FEED and FEED studies, as assigned by the Head of TFC, in line with experience and expertise.
    3. Participate in technical meetings with partners, suppliers, research institutions and other collaborators.
    4. Collaborate closely with other engineering disciplines and contribute to the integration of TFC systems within the wider fusion plant.
    5. As required, undertake other relevant duties in support of project objectives.
  • GID-170 delivery (in the 2030s)
    1. Support the procurement and installation activities of the GID-170 TFC facilities.
    2. Develop commissioning plans and operating instructions.
The balance between process design, systems engineering, and process modelling and simulation will depend on each candidate’s background and area of expertise. All engineers are expected to work collaboratively across these areas, ensuring that modelling activities inform engineering decisions and that process design is supported by robust analysis.


Qualification and educational requirements

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in chemical engineering, process engineering, nuclear engineering, or a closely related discipline*. 

*In the case of a closely related discipline, the degree should be supported by relevant chemical engineering experience.

  • A minimum of 3 years design experience working as a Process Engineer in an industrial environment.

    Additional desirable qualifications relevant to process modelling and simulation:
  • A PhD or EngD in Chemical or Process Engineering or a closely related field.


Competences and preferred skills

1. Common skills

Essential

All applicants should demonstrate:

  • In-depth knowledge of chemical engineering principles, including thermodynamics, heat and mass transfer, process dynamics, and relevant transport phenomena.
  • Experience in the development of industrial-scale process engineering installations in complex environments requiring regulatory approval (ideally nuclear projects or similar).
  • Experience in the development of processes involving different fluids and conditions (cryogenic, vacuum, atmospheric pressure gas, high-pressure gas (up to 100 bara), liquid, etc.).
  • Experience in the design and development of integrated treatment unit operations (purification, separation, conditioning, etc.), ideally in the gas phase, and in the hydrogen or nuclear sectors.
  • Proficiency in at least one established process simulation tool, such as Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, UniSim, gPROMS, ProMax, CHEMCAD or equivalent.
  • Experience in requirements capture, documentation and management.
  • Experience working alongside multiple other engineering disciplines, such as mechanical, electrical, control, thermal and nuclear engineers.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams of engineers, technologists and physicists.
  • A proactive and self-motivated approach, with strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills.
  • Professional working proficiency in English. 

Desirable

All applicants would benefit from demonstrating:

  • Knowledge of tritium fuel cycle technologies and/or hydrogen isotope separation. Hands-on experience working with tritium would be an advantage.
  • Experience with the design or analysis of pumping technologies, heat exchangers or other key process equipment.
  • Familiarity with magnetic fusion systems and/or nuclear power plant systems.
  • Familiarity with environmental, nuclear safety and other relevant regulatory requirements. 
  • Knowledge of systems engineering and an understanding of configuration management and risk management.
  • Understanding of equipment qualification, manufacture, testing, inspection and pragmatic usability.
  • Knowledge of German or other European languages.

2. Specialist Skills

Candidates are expected to demonstrate strengths in one or more of the following areas, depending on their background and specialisation.

Process design and systems engineering

  • Experience in developing process architectures, heat and mass balances, PFDs and P&IDs, and in supporting equipment selection, sizing and integration.
  • Experience in developing Basis of Design (BoD) documentation, design philosophies, specifications, design descriptions and justifications.
  • Ability to assess alternative process technologies and configurations, considering performance, safety, technical maturity and operational requirements.
  • Experience in translating system requirements and process analysis into engineering specifications and design decisions.
  • Familiarity with process safety codes, standards and regulations, as well as safety-by-design principles, including the ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) approach.
  • Experience in engaging with potential technology suppliers and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs).

Process modelling and simulation

  • Proficiency in process modelling tools such as Aspen Custom Modeler, gPROMS custom modelling or equivalent.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming or scientific computing language, such as Python, Julia, MATLAB, Octave or C++.
  • Strong understanding of numerical methods applied to chemical engineering, including ordinary and partial differential equations (ODEs and PDEs), differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), discretisation techniques and numerical convergence.
  • Knowledge of numerical optimisation methods and their implementation, with the ability to apply them to process analysis and design optimisation.
  • Experience developing custom process models, integrating subsystem models or analysing dynamic process behaviour, along with model automation and analysis, to assess system performance, compare design options and support process optimisation is an advantage.


We are recruiting engineers with complementary technical strengths. Applicants who meet the common essential criteria and have relevant capability in one specialist profile are encouraged to apply; experience in every technology or software package listed is not expected.


The balance of responsibilities and the level of technical ownership will be agreed according to each successful candidate’s experience and the needs of the programme, with opportunities for candidates to grow and develop into greater technical ownership.

Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job.

You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them):

  • Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing.

  • Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout.

Own the customer success and value plan

  • Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

  • Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

  • Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

Make deployment realities part of the success plan

  • Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

  • Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

  • Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

  • Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

  • Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

  • Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

  • Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

  • Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes.

Defend and grow the commercial relationship

  • Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time.

  • Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value.

  • Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks.

Bring the customer voice into Mistral

  • Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions.

Build the company as well as the account

  • Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions.

  • Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it.
